relations.definition: Indicates the geographical location where an event took place
relations.embedding_query_text: occurred in: Indicates the geographical location where an event took place

chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: The 'location' property fits as WildfireEvent (Event) → Country (Place) aligns with its domain/range.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

relations.definition: Describes a geographical area affected by an event
relations.embedding_query_text: impacted: Describes a geographical area affected by an event

chosen_property.label: affectedArea
chosen_property.definition: A geographical area affected by an event.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property directly expresses WildfireEvent → City as an impact relation; 'affectedArea' is minted to capture this.

candidates.label: affectedBy
candidates.comment: An affected by relation between a medical test and the drugs that can influence its results. Also called influenced by, impacted by, drug interaction. Examples: "A blood test's results are affected by 'anticoagulants'.", "The diagnostic test is affected by 'caffeine'."

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: geographicArea
candidates.comment: A geographic area relation between an audience and the administrative area it is associated with. Also called: target region, audience location, demographic area. Examples: "Local News Audience" geographic area "Springfield County", "National Election Voters" geographic area "United States", "European Market Audience" geographic area "European Union".

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: spatialCoverage
candidates.comment: A geographic focus relation between a creative work and the place(s) that are the primary subject or focus of its content. Also called "geographic scope", "covered area", "location focus", "content location". Examples: "A weather dataset has spatialCoverage New York State", "The historical map's spatialCoverage is ancient Rome", "This research paper's spatialCoverage is the Arctic region.". Distinct from spatial, which is a more general spatial association when the specific focus is not known.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: area
candidates.comment: An area relation between a broadcast service and the geographic place where its users can access it. Also called service region, coverage area, broadcast zone. Examples: "A radio station's area is 'Greater London'.", "The TV service's area is 'North America'."

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

relations.definition: Specifies the administrative or geographical division containing an entity
relations.embedding_query_text: located in: Specifies the administrative or geographical division containing an entity

chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: The 'location' property fits as WildfireEvent (Event) → DefinedRegion/City (Place) aligns with its domain/range.

candidates.label: addressRegion
candidates.comment: An address region relation between a defined region or postal address and the administrative division (e.g., state, province) it belongs to. Also called state, province, administrative area. Examples: "A postal address's address region is 'CA'.", "The address region is 'Bavaria'."

candidates.label: geoWithin
candidates.comment: A geo within relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is located entirely inside the interior of another containing geometry or place. Also called: is inside, contained in, located within. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo within "Country 'France'", "Office 'Suite 100'" geo within "Building 'Empire State'", "State 'California'" geo within "Country 'USA'". Distinct from geoContains, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: geographicArea
candidates.comment: A geographic area relation between an audience and the administrative area it is associated with. Also called: target region, audience location, demographic area. Examples: "Local News Audience" geographic area "Springfield County", "National Election Voters" geographic area "United States", "European Market Audience" geographic area "European Union".

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: legalAddress
candidates.comment: An official location relation between an organization and its legally registered postal address for administrative and tax purposes. Also called registered address, official address, corporate address, statutory address. Examples: An organization has a legalAddress of '100 Main St, Anytown, USA'. A company's legalAddress is 'Suite 200, Business Park, City'. The corporation's legalAddress is its registered office. Distinct from address, which is a general contact address, and branchOf, which is about organizational hierarchy.

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: serviceArea
candidates.comment: The geographical region or area where a service is available or provided. Also called service region, coverage area, operational zone. Examples: `Delivery Service` serviceArea `GeoShape: New York City`, `Local Business` serviceArea `AdministrativeArea: California`, `Customer Support` serviceArea `Place: United States`. Distinct from `areaServed`, which is a more general property for things like organizations.

relations.definition: Indicates a direct consequence or outcome of an event
relations.embedding_query_text: resulted in: Indicates a direct consequence or outcome of an event

chosen_property.label: result
chosen_property.justification: WildfireEvent (Action) → Quantity/DefinedRegion (Thing) matches the 'result' property's domain/range.

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: resultReview
candidates.comment: The specific review created as the outcome of a review action. Also called generated review, review outcome, produced review. Examples: `ReviewAction on Product` resultReview `Customer's Product Review`, `ReviewAction on Movie` resultReview `Critic's Movie Review`, `ReviewAction on Service` resultReview `User Service Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: afterMedia
candidates.comment: An after media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL depicting the state or circumstances after completing that step. Also called post-step media, result image, outcome visual. Examples: "A recipe direction's after media is an image of the mixed ingredients.", "The assembly instruction's after media is a video of the connected parts."

relations.definition: Indicates a benchmark or reference for comparison
relations.embedding_query_text: comparative to: Indicates a benchmark or reference for comparison

chosen_property.label: comparativeReferenceTime
chosen_property.definition: A benchmark or reference time period for comparison.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property matches DefinedRegion → Date for a comparative relation; 'comparativeReferenceTime' is minted.

candidates.label: referenceQuantity
candidates.comment: A reference quantity relation between a unit price specification and the specific quantity for which the stated price applies. Also called quantity for price, price per quantity. Examples: "A electricity price specification has a reference quantity '4 kWh'.", "A bulk discount has a reference quantity '10 units'.", "A service charge has a reference quantity '1 hour'."

candidates.label: valueReference
candidates.comment: A value reference relation between a property value, qualitative value, or quantitative value and a secondary value providing additional information or context. Also called reference value, contextual value, measurement context. Examples: "QuantitativeValue valueReference 'Standard Temperature'", "PropertyValue valueReference 'Color Spectrum'", "QuantitativeValue valueReference 'RPM at max torque'".

candidates.label: lesserOrEqual
candidates.comment: A lesser or equal ordering relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject value is smaller than or equal to the object value. Also called: is less than or equal to, is at most, does not exceed. Examples: "Low lesserOrEqual Medium", "Small lesserOrEqual Small", "Cold lesserOrEqual Cold". Distinct from lesser, which strictly indicates a smaller value.

candidates.label: greaterOrEqual
candidates.comment: A greater or equal relation indicating that one qualitative value is superior to or the same as another. Also called: is greater than or equal to, at least, no less than. Examples: "High" greater or equal "Medium", "Good" greater or equal "Good", "Large" greater or equal "Medium". Distinct from greater, which does not include equality.

candidates.label: greater
candidates.comment: A greater relation indicating that one qualitative value is superior or larger than another. Also called: is greater than, exceeds, is more than. Examples: "High" greater "Medium", "Excellent" greater "Good", "Large" greater "Small". Distinct from greaterOrEqual, which includes equality.

candidates.label: lesser
candidates.comment: A lesser ordering relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject value is smaller than the object value. Also called: is less than, is smaller than, falls below. Examples: "Low lesser Medium", "Small lesser Large", "Cold lesser Warm". Distinct from lesserOrEqual, which includes equality.

candidates.label: equal
candidates.comment: An equality relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject qualitative value is considered equal to the object qualitative value within a specific ordering context. Also called "is equivalent to", "is the same as", "matches". Examples: "Qualitative value 'Satisfactory' equal 'Acceptable'", "Qualitative value 'Medium' equal 'Average'", "Qualitative value 'High' equal 'Very Good'".

candidates.label: citation
candidates.comment: A reference relation between a creative work and another creative work or text that it cites. Also called "reference", "cited work", "source". Examples: "Research paper citation 'Smith, J. (2020). Article Title.'", "Blog post citation 'https://example.com/article'".

candidates.label: ratingValue
candidates.comment: A rating value relation between a rating and its numerical or textual score. Also called score, rating score, value of rating. Examples: "A movie review has a rating value of 4.5.", "A product has a rating value of 'Excellent'.", "A restaurant has a rating value of 3 stars."

candidates.label: referencesOrder
candidates.comment: A references order relation between an invoice and the order(s) it pertains to. Also called related order, invoice for order. Examples: "An invoice references order 'Order #123'.", "A billing statement references order 'multiple orders'.", "A payment request references order 'Subscription Renewal'."

relations.definition: Connects an official to a public declaration they issued
relations.embedding_query_text: made statement: Connects an official to a public declaration they issued

instances: Laurent Nunez -> French Interior Minister describes fire intensity
Pedro Sanchez -> Spanish Prime Minister assesses fire situation

chosen_property.label: issuedStatement
chosen_property.definition: Connects an official to a public declaration they issued.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property matches GovernmentOfficial → OfficialStatement for a statement issuance; 'issuedStatement' is minted.

candidates.label: copyrightNotice
candidates.comment: A textual declaration relation between a creative work and the statement describing its copyright aspects. Also called: copyright statement, copyright declaration, copyright text. Examples: "My Novel" copyright notice "© 2023 John Doe", "Company Website" copyright notice "Copyright 2023 Example Corp. All Rights Reserved.", "Academic Paper" copyright notice "Published under CC BY 4.0 license". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which identifies the entity owning the copyright.

candidates.label: issuedBy
candidates.comment: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. Also called granted by, provided by, authorized by, issuer. Examples: A driver's license is issuedBy 'Department of Motor Vehicles'. A concert ticket is issuedBy 'Ticketmaster'. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.

candidates.label: legislationIdentifier
candidates.comment: An identifier relation between a piece of legislation and its unique string or URL-based identifier. Also called: legal identifier, official ID, legislative code. Examples: "EU Regulation 2016/679 legislationIdentifier CELEX:32016R0679", "French Law legislationIdentifier NOR:XXXXXX", "UK Act legislationIdentifier URN-Lex:XXXX".

candidates.label: publicAccess
candidates.comment: A public access relation indicating whether a place is open to public visitors. Also called open to public, publicly accessible. Examples: "A park has public access 'true'.", "A private residence has public access 'false'.", "A museum has public access 'true'."

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: legalRepresentative
candidates.comment: A legal representation relation between an organization and the person(s) authorized to act on its behalf in legal matters. Also called authorized representative, legal agent, official representative, corporate officer. Examples: An organization has a legalRepresentative of 'its CEO'. A company's legalRepresentative is 'its sole administrator'. The board appointed 'Jane Doe' as legalRepresentative. Distinct from employee, which is a general employment relation, not specifically legal representation.

candidates.label: legislationCountersignedBy
candidates.comment: A countersignature relation between a piece of legislation and the person or organization that countersigned it. Also called: countersigned by, officially endorsed by, co-signed by. Examples: "The Bill of Rights legislationCountersignedBy President Washington", "EU Directive 2023/45 legislationCountersignedBy European Commission", "Local Ordinance legislationCountersignedBy City Clerk".

candidates.label: issuedThrough
candidates.comment: A service channel relation between a permit and the specific service used to obtain it. Also called obtained via, granted through, service channel. Examples: A building permit was issuedThrough 'Online Permit Application System'. A fishing license was issuedThrough 'State Wildlife Service'. A visa was issuedThrough 'Consular Services Department'. Distinct from issuedBy, which is the organization, not the service.

candidates.label: legalName
candidates.comment: An official identification relation between an organization and its formally registered name. Also called registered name, official company name, corporate name, full legal name. Examples: An organization has a legalName of 'Acme Corporation Inc.'. A company's legalName is 'Global Solutions LLC'. The charity's legalName is 'Helping Hands Foundation'. Distinct from name, which is the common or display name.

candidates.label: publicTransportClosuresInfo
candidates.comment: A public transport closures information relation between a special announcement and details regarding public transport disruptions. Also called transport closure details, public transit alerts. Examples: "A special announcement includes public transport closures info about subway lines.", "An emergency alert provides public transport closures info for bus routes.", "A news update contains public transport closures info for train services."

relations.definition: Establishes a contextual connection between two facts
relations.embedding_query_text: related to: Establishes a contextual connection between two facts

instances: French Interior Minister describes fire intensity -> Wildfires in France

chosen_property.label: relatedEvent
chosen_property.definition: Establishes a contextual connection between an official statement and a wildfire event.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property matches OfficialStatement → WildfireEvent as a contextual link; 'relatedEvent' is minted.

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: follows
candidates.comment: A follows relation representing a generic uni-directional social connection between two people. Also called: is following, subscribes to, tracks. Examples: "Alice follows Bob", "Charlie follows David", "Eve follows Frank". Distinct from followee, which is the object of a follow action.

candidates.label: valueReference
candidates.comment: A value reference relation between a property value, qualitative value, or quantitative value and a secondary value providing additional information or context. Also called reference value, contextual value, measurement context. Examples: "QuantitativeValue valueReference 'Standard Temperature'", "PropertyValue valueReference 'Color Spectrum'", "QuantitativeValue valueReference 'RPM at max torque'".

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. candidates.label: relatedLink
candidates.comment: A related link relation between a web page and a URL pointing to another relevant web page. Also called external link, associated link, further reading. Examples: "A news article has a related link to 'the source report'.", "A product page has a related link to 'customer reviews'.", "A blog post has a related link to 'a previous article'."

candidates.label: connectedTo
candidates.comment: A connection relation between an anatomical structure and other anatomical structures it is connected to. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "connects with". Examples: "Femur anatomical structure connectedTo Tibia", "Brain anatomical structure connectedTo Spinal cord".

candidates.label: spatial

candidates.label: relatedStructure

candidates.label: relatedCondition
candidates.comment: A related condition relation between an anatomical structure or system and a medical condition associated with it. Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: endDate
candidates.comment: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.

candidates.label: coverageEndTime
candidates.comment: A temporal boundary relation between a live blog posting and the time when its event coverage concludes. Also called: coverage end, reporting end time, live blog conclusion. Examples: "Election Night Live Blog" coverage end time "2024-11-06T04:00:00Z", "Sports Event Live Update" coverage end time "2023-07-15T19:30:00Z", "Conference Live Blog" coverage end time "2023-10-27T17:00:00Z". Distinct from coverageStartTime, which indicates when coverage begins.

candidates.label: eventSchedule
candidates.comment: An event schedule relation between an event and a schedule that defines a series of repeating occurrences for it. Also called "recurring schedule", "event timetable", "series schedule". Examples: "Gym class eventSchedule 'Weekly schedule for Yoga'", "Concert series eventSchedule 'Schedule for monthly performances'", "Webinar series eventSchedule 'Schedule for bi-weekly sessions'". Distinct from schedule, which is a more general property for any schedule.

candidates.label: vehicleTransmission
candidates.comment: A vehicle transmission relation between a vehicle and the type of component used for transmitting power to the wheels. Also called transmission type, gearbox type, drivetrain. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Automatic'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Manual'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Continuously Variable Transmission'".

candidates.label: object
candidates.comment: A thing upon which an action is carried out, potentially changing its state. Also called target, item acted upon, recipient of action. Examples: "Read Action object 'a book'", "Buy Action object 'a product'", "Edit Action object 'a document'". Distinct from instrument, which is the tool used to perform the action.

candidates.label: deliveryStatus
candidates.comment: A logistical progress relation between a parcel delivery and the events marking its journey from shipment to final delivery. Also called: shipment status, package status, tracking updates. Examples: "Package" delivery status "In Transit", "Order" delivery status "Out for Delivery", "Shipment" delivery status "Delivered".

candidates.label: hasDeliveryMethod
candidates.comment: A delivery method relation between a delivery event or parcel delivery and the method used for its delivery. Also called delivery via, shipping method, method of delivery. Examples: "A parcel delivery has a delivery method of 'express shipping'.", "The delivery event has a delivery method of 'pickup'.", "The order uses a delivery method of 'standard mail'."

candidates.label: serviceArea
candidates.comment: The geographical region or area where a service is available or provided. Also called service region, coverage area, operational zone. Examples: `Delivery Service` serviceArea `GeoShape: New York City`, `Local Business` serviceArea `AdministrativeArea: California`, `Customer Support` serviceArea `Place: United States`. Distinct from `areaServed`, which is a more general property for things like organizations.

candidates.label: specialCommitments
candidates.comment: A description of any specific commitments or considerations associated with a job posting. Also called "job commitments", "employment considerations", "special hiring programs". Examples: "The job posting has specialCommitments VeteranCommit", "This role includes specialCommitments for military spouses", "The company lists specialCommitments for diversity initiatives."

candidates.label: arrivalPlatform
candidates.comment: A platform identification for a train trip's arrival location. Also called: train arrival platform, destination platform. Examples: "TrainTrip 123 arrivalPlatform 'Platform 7'", "TrainTrip to London arrivalPlatform 'Track 1'", "TrainTrip from Paris arrivalPlatform 'Gate C'."

candidates.label: issuedThrough
candidates.comment: A service channel relation between a permit and the specific service used to obtain it. Also called obtained via, granted through, service channel. Examples: A building permit was issuedThrough 'Online Permit Application System'. A fishing license was issuedThrough 'State Wildlife Service'. A visa was issuedThrough 'Consular Services Department'. Distinct from issuedBy, which is the organization, not the service.

candidates.label: availableDeliveryMethod
candidates.comment: A delivery method available for an offer. Also called: shipping option, delivery option, fulfillment method. Examples: "Offer 'Product Z' availableDeliveryMethod 'DeliveryMode.Shipping'", "Offer 'Food' availableDeliveryMethod 'DeliveryMode.Pickup'."

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".
